canonical.name: This low pair defines completion entirely through inverse limits of compatible residue systems; it does not introduce a Cauchy-sequence quotient or any formal-power-series construction on the A page.
On this page, a complete filtered module is separated by definition and is identified by the canonical map to the inverse limit of its filtered quotients.
Inverse-limit exactness is stated only in the countable Mittag-Leffler form, with the derived $\varprojlim^1$ obstruction kept outside this low commutative-algebra spine.
Completion exactness and the tensor comparison are only asserted for finite modules over Noetherian rings; the companion page keeps the nonfinite failure explicit.
Flatness of Noetherian completion is proved through the tensor comparison plus the ideal criterion for flatness, not through Tor.
Faithful flatness is not claimed for arbitrary adic completion maps: the Jacobson-radical hypothesis is load-bearing and remains explicit in both the theorem and the notes.

The local comparison theorem is limited to Noetherian local rings and finite modules, and the final Hilbert-Samuel comparison is routed through the batch-2 Artin-Rees and Hilbert-Samuel machinery rather than silently internalized here.
